item.title: James Gray Says New York Has “Run Its Course” With His Films & Talks Finding Joy In The Tragedy Of ‘Paper Tiger’ [Interview]
item.description: James Gray has spent much of his filmmaking career returning to New York. From the Brighton Beach streets of “ Little Odessa ,” his 1994 debut, to “ The Yards ,” “ We Own The Night ,” “ Two Lovers ,” “ The Immigrant ,” and “ Armageddon Time ,” the city has remained a constant presence in his work. It is a striking attachment for a filmmaker who has lived in Los Angeles since 2012, and whose films have also taken him into the Amazon with “ The Lost City Of Z ” and into space with Brad Pitt in “ Ad Astra ” (which he talked about more at length in this interview excerpt). item.title: James Gray Says He’s “Dying” To Make An ‘Ad Astra’ Director’s Cut & Has Had Conversations With The Criterion Collection
item.description: Seven years after the release of “ Ad Astra ,” filmmaker James Gray remains eager to revisit his ambitious science-fiction drama starring Brad Pitt .
